props.title: Se7en
props.initialSlug: Seven deadly sins. One deadly game.

sections.content: Se7en revolutionized the serial killer thriller by plunging viewers into a nightmarish urban hell where evil methodically unfolds through the seven deadly sins. Director David Fincher's breakthrough film pairs veteran detective Somerset (Morgan Freeman) with volatile newcomer Mills (Brad Pitt) as they track a killer staging elaborate murder tableaus. The film's oppressive atmosphere, created through constant rain and darkness, builds unbearable tension that influenced countless subsequent thrillers like 8MM (1999) and Saw (2004). Fincher's meticulous attention to detail and Andrew Kevin Walker's twisted screenplay created a new template for psychological horror.

sections.content: The film's technical innovation can't be overstated. Cinematographer Darius Khondji created a bleach bypass process that gave Se7en its signature gritty look, influencing the visual style of The Game (1997) and Fight Club (1999). The opening credits sequence by Kyle Cooper revolutionized title design, spawning countless imitators. Even the marketing campaign broke new ground by refusing to reveal the contents of the infamous box, building word-of-mouth through mystery.

Beyond its craft, Se7en tapped into millennial anxiety about urban decay and moral rot. Like Taxi Driver (1976) before it, the film presents a city beyond redemption. The killer John Doe sees himself as a prophet punishing sin, echoing real-world religious extremism. This theme of righteous violence would later appear in films like Frailty (2001) and Red Dragon (2002). SUBHEAD: Legacy and Influence

movies.title: Gone Girl
movies.slug: Another Fincher thriller about appearances versus reality when a wife mysteriously disappears

sections.content: The film's ending remains one of cinema's most shocking conclusions, subverting audience expectations of justice or redemption. This nihilistic finish influenced a wave of dark endings in films like Arlington Road (1999) and The Mist (2007). The partnership between the seasoned cop and hotheaded rookie became a template for countless police thrillers, though few achieved Se7en's perfect chemistry between Freeman and Pitt.

Se7en's influence extends beyond thriller conventions. Its vision of evil as methodical and intellectual rather than merely psychotic shaped films like Copycat (1995) and Taking Lives (2004). The killer's elaborate crime scenes prefigured the "murder as art" concept in shows like Hannibal (2013-2015) and movies like The Cell (2000).
